review: The hymn is Philippians 4:4–6 with Hebrews 13:5–6: 1:1–4 is Phil 4:4 with Ps 126:1 (הָיִינוּ כְּחֹלְמִים), 2:1–4 Phil 4:5–6, 3:1–4 Phil 4:7, 4:1–4 Heb 13:5 with 1 Tim 6:8, and 5:1–6:4 Heb 13:5–6 quoting Deut 31:6 and Ps 118:7.

1:3 כְּאַנְשֵׁי חֲלוֹם נִהְיֶה — the Arabic وَكَأُنَاسٍ حُلُمًا is 'as men dreaming', which is Ps 126:1's כְּחֹלְמִים; the Hebrew keeps the fuller construct כְּאַנְשֵׁי חֲלוֹם rather than the psalm's single word, because the line has to carry both halves of the Arabic (the men and the dream) and the psalm's phrase alone would be four syllables short.

2:2 נִשְׁקְדָה בַתְּפִלָּה — the Arabic فَلْنَصْحُ لِلصَّلَاة is 'let us wake for prayer'; the Hebrew uses שָׁקַד, the verb of watching and staying awake (Jer 1:12, שֹׁקֵד אֲנִי עַל־דְּבָרִי), so the line keeps the vigilance of the Arabic and not merely the act of praying.

4:1–2 דַּרְכֵּנוּ לִהְיוֹת חָפְשִׁי / מֵאַהֲבַת הַכֶּסֶף — the Arabic سَبِيلُنَا أَنْ نَخْلُو مِنْ / مَحَبَّةٍ لِلْمَال breaks the phrase across the two printed lines; the Hebrew follows the break, so the couplet still says 'free — from the love of money', and the enjambment is the stanza's form.

5:1 לֹא אֶעֱזֹב וְלֹא אֶרְפֶּה — the Arabic لَا أُهْمِلُ لَا أَتْرُكُ is Heb 13:5's οὐ μή σε ἀνῶ; the Hebrew keeps both verbs and the first person, because the stanza is quoting the promise as God's own speech and then answering it in 5:4 with the psalm's אֲדֹנָי עֶזְרִי.
